lessons.title: Personal hygiene on the farm
lessons.html:
Personal hygiene on the farm

Hygiene means keeping things clean to stop germs (bacteria, viruses and parasites) from spreading. On a farm, germs can spread from animals to people, from people to food, and from one animal group to another. Good hygiene protects your health, the health of animals, and the safety of the food we produce.

Why it matters

  • Some animal diseases infect people, such as brucellosis, anthrax, ringworm and Salmonella.
  • Dirty hands can contaminate fruit, vegetables, milk and eggs. Buyers and export markets check this strictly.
  • Clean workers and clean equipment reduce disease in animals and crops.

Personal hygiene rules

  • Wash your hands with soap and clean water: before starting work, before eating, after using the toilet, after handling animals, manure, chemicals or rubbish, and after breaks.
  • Keep nails short and clean. Cover cuts and sores with a waterproof plaster.
  • Wear clean work clothes and the PPE given to you. Change clothes after working with chemicals.
  • Use the toilets provided. Never relieve yourself in the orchard, field or near water.
  • Do not eat, drink, smoke or chew gum in packing areas, dairies or while handling chemicals.
  • Tell your supervisor if you have diarrhoea, vomiting, fever or an infected wound. You may need to do other work for a while.
  • Cough or sneeze into your elbow or a tissue, away from produce.

How to wash hands properly

  1. Wet hands with clean running water.
  2. Apply soap.
  3. Rub palms, backs of hands, between fingers, thumbs and under nails for about 20 seconds.
  4. Rinse well under running water.
  5. Dry with a single-use paper towel. Do not dry hands on your clothes.

Field toilets and hand-wash stations must be kept stocked with soap, water and paper towels. Report when they are empty or dirty.

lessons.title: Hygiene of work areas, equipment and animals
lessons.html:
Hygiene of work areas, equipment and animals

Cleaning and disinfecting

Cleaning removes dirt, dung and food remains. Disinfecting (sanitising) kills germs that remain. Disinfectants do not work well on dirty surfaces, so always clean first.

  1. Remove loose dirt, manure and waste.
  2. Wash with water and detergent; scrub.
  3. Rinse with clean water.
  4. Apply the disinfectant at the strength on the label, for the contact time on the label.
  5. Rinse if the label says so, and let surfaces dry.

Areas and equipment to keep clean

  • Picking crates, bins, knives and scissors.
  • Pack house tables, conveyors and cold rooms.
  • Milking parlours, milking machines and milk tanks.
  • Feeders, drinkers and water troughs.
  • Animal houses, pens and kraals.
  • Toilets, hand-wash stations and staff kitchens.

Biosecurity for animals

Biosecurity means keeping diseases out and stopping them from spreading on the farm.

  • Use foot baths at the entrance to poultry and pig houses; keep them topped up with disinfectant.
  • Wear separate boots and overalls for each house where required.
  • Keep visitors and vehicles out of animal areas unless allowed.
  • Keep new and sick animals separate.
  • Remove dead animals quickly and dispose of them as instructed.
  • Control rats, mice, flies and wild birds.

Waste management

  • Put rubbish in bins with lids; empty them regularly.
  • Keep food waste away from animal feed and water.
  • Store manure away from water sources and packing areas.
  • Never throw chemical containers or waste into rivers or dams.

Chemical safety

Cleaning chemicals can burn skin and eyes. Wear gloves and eye protection, never mix products (some mixtures release poisonous gas), and store them in their original labelled containers away from food.

Key points

  • Hygiene stops germs spreading between animals, people and food.
  • Wash hands with soap at the right times, for about 20 seconds.
  • Report illness such as diarrhoea or infected wounds to your supervisor.
  • Clean first, then disinfect at the label strength and contact time.
  • Follow biosecurity rules, manage waste, and never mix cleaning chemicals.
